chapters.summary: Council staff opens the Committee on Immigration hearing, asks attendees to silence electronic devices, and explains how to sign up for in-person testimony. Staff then tells the chair the committee is ready to begin.
chapters.title: Council staff opens hearing and gives housekeeping instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Welcome to today's hearing from the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, I would like to remind everyone to silence all electronic devices.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Also, at this point, going forward, no one is to approach the days.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: If you would like to sign up for in-person testimony, please see one of the sergeants at arms.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair, we're ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Chair Elsie Encarnación calls the hearing to order, introduces herself as chair of the Committee on Immigration, and states that the committee will examine Executive Order 13 of 2026 and its audit findings. She thanks administration representatives, the public, and colleagues for attending.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación calls hearing to order and introduces EO 13 oversight

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am calling this hearing to order.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am Councilmember Elsie Encarnacion, Deputy Whip of the New York City Council and Chair of the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you all for joining us today.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Today we will be examining the Executive Order 13 of 2026 Report and Audit Findings and Recommendations.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación frames New York City's sanctuary legacy, noting local laws since 2011 that restrict city resources from facilitating federal immigration enforcement. She says these safeguards are meant to uphold the dignity of all residents.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación frames New York City's sanctuary legacy

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'd like to thank all of the representatives from the administration, members of the public, and my council colleagues who have joined us here today, including Council Member Lewis.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: New York City has a proud legacy of restricting the use of city time or property to facilitate federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Local laws enacted by the council since 2011 have directed city resources away from the enforcement of xenophobic federal immigration policies and the agencies that weaponize them.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: These safeguards ensure that the city does not conduct civil immigration enforcement and that it instead upholds the dignity of all residents of our sanctuary city.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: But laws are only as good as their enforcement and implementation.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación cites Department of Investigation reports from late 2025 detailing violations of detainer laws by DOC and NYPD. She also notes public reporting that ICE entered city shelters armed and without judicial warrants at least five times in 2025.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación cites DOI reports and armed ICE shelter incidents

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In late 2025, the city's Department of Investigation released two reports detailing violations of the city's detainer laws by the New York City Department.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: and the Department of Correction.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Public reporting also revealed that Immigration and Customs Enforcement had entered New York City shelters armed and without judicial warrants at least five times in 2025.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: To be a true sanctuary city, our residents must trust that the city will uphold its protective local laws.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación explains that Mayor Mamdani issued Executive Order 13 on February 6, 2026, requiring six agencies to audit compliance with local immigration laws. She describes the order's requirement to submit a report within 90 days and its creation of an interagency response committee.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación outlines Executive Order 13 requirements

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: That's why I was extremely pleased when on February 6, 2026, the Mamdani administration issued Executive Order 13, protecting New Yorkers from abusive immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The EO required that the Administration for Children's Services, Department of Correction,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Department of Health and Mental Hygiene, Department of Probation, Department of Social Services, and the New York City Police Department

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: to ensure compliance with all relevant laws, rules, procedures, guidelines, and reporting requirements related to non-local immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The EO ordered the agencies to immediately conduct a review and audit all internal policies, guidelines, and protocols related to communication,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: cooperation, and coordination with non-local law enforcement agencies charged with immigration enforcement and submit a report to the mayor within 90 days.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The EO also established an interagency response.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: committee, and moving forward, I will refer to it as the IRC, to coordinate and manage policy response across agencies for any crisis in the city of New York.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación summarizes the May 22 audit report, which found intensified federal targeting of city shelters and increased detainer requests to DOC and NYPD. She says the mayor adopted agency-specific recommendations to strengthen protections.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación summarizes May 22 audit findings

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: On May 22nd, the administration released the Executive Order 13 audit.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Report of audit findings and recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Among other findings, the multi-agency order revealed that federal immigration authorities had intensified their targeting of city shelters, sharply increased the issuance of detainer requests to DOC and NYPD,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: and employed increasingly aggressive and misleading tactics.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The mayor adopted several agency-specific recommendations to strengthen policies and protocols to respond to the changing landscape of federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The administration stated that in the coming months, the city would implement recommendations from the audit to strengthen protections for immigrant New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: The administration also noted that the IRC would issue updated citywide guidance and work closely with agencies to implement these policies and protocol changes.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación says the hearing will assess implementation of the audit recommendations and how the administration will communicate progress. She says the committee will question MOIA about its IRC role, guidance timeline, and work with agencies.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación states hearing purpose and MOIA questions

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: At this hearing, we will assess the administration's implementation of the recommendations from the audit and ascertain how the administration intends to communicate its process.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Progress to the public.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We will question the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs about its role on the IRC, the timeline for issuing updated citywide guidance,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: and the nature of the office's work with agencies to implement the policy and protocol changes.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Although it seeks to examine a report of audit findings and recommendations, this hearing is not merely an academic exercise.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: If properly implemented, enforced, and resourced, the recommendations contained in this report would be game-changing for the immigrant residents of our city.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: This committee takes our community's trust in government and willingness to access city resources extremely seriously.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And so we understand the high stakes of getting this right.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We are holding this hearing today to ensure that the administration's report is not the end of the work to uphold the safety and well-being of our city's immigrant population, but rather that it signifies the beginning of that work.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación introduces Resolution 626, sponsored by Council Member Farah Louis, calling on the U.S. Senate to pass S.4814 to designate Haiti for Temporary Protected Status. She notes Haiti's instability since the 2010 earthquake and says she is proud to co-sponsor the resolution.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación introduces Resolution 626 on Haiti TPS

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Lastly, the Committee on Immigration will hear Resolution 626, sponsored by Councilmember Farrah Lewis, calling upon the United States Senate to pass and the President to sign

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: S.4814 to require the Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protective status.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Haiti has experienced a great deal of instability since the 2010 earthquake, including an epidemic, another earthquake, and tropical storm.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm actually going to let, because I know you have a few words on this, so I'll let you kind of get into the actual resolution.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I...

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm also proud to co-sponsor this resolution, and I thank you, Councilmember Lewis, for introducing it.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks committee staff, including Senior Legislative Counsel Nicole Cata and policy and finance analysts, for their work on the hearing. She also thanks her own staff, especially Chief of Staff Stephanie Herrera, and the Sergeant at Arms.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación thanks committee and personal staff

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I would also like to thank the committee staff for their work on this hearing, including Senior Legislative Counsel Nicole Cata,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Senior Legislative Policy Analyst Rebecca Barilla, Principal Financial Analyst Navi Baines, and Assistant Finance Director Florentine Kabor.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Finally, I would like to thank my staff, especially my Chief of Staff, Stephanie Herrera, and everyone working behind the scenes to make this hearing run smoothly, including our amazing Sergeant at Arms.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación turns the floor to Council Member Farah Louis for remarks on Resolution 626. Louis thanks the chair, greets Commissioner Ali, and acknowledges advocates including the Haitian American Lawyers Association and 1199.
chapters.title: Council Member Lewis begins remarks on Resolution 626

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to Councilmember Lewis for brief remarks on her bill.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair and Connoisseur, for your support of this resolution and for convening today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Good to see you, Commissioner Ali.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And I want to thank some of the advocates that are here today, the Haitian American Lawyers Association of New York.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: You have President Rodney Pippe here and Cheryl John from 1199.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I want to begin by saying this plainly.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Resol 626 is personal to me, Haitian Americans, to the broader Black diaspora in New York City, and to every friend and ally of the Haitian community.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I am a proud Haitian-Bahamian American woman representing one of the largest Haitian diaspora communities in the United States, in central Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: When I speak about TPS recipients, I'm not speaking about statistics.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I'm speaking about my neighbors, my constituents, my family.

chapters.summary: Council Member Louis tells the story of her cousin Pierre Richard Eloy, who was days away from receiving TPS and traveling to New York when he was murdered in Haiti. She says TPS termination is life-or-death for Haitian families and describes the case of a Haitian student placed on an ankle monitor.
chapters.title: Council Member Lewis recounts cousin's murder after TPS approval

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I want to tell you about my cousin.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: His name was Pierre Richard Eloy.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: In August 2024, Pierre Richard was days away from boarding a flight to New York City.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: He had just received confirmation that he would be granted temporary protected status, also known as TPS.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Word got out to his community that he was leaving.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And because he refused to join the barbecue gang, they murdered him.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Ten bullets in front of his own home, in front of his family.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: They held his body for ransom.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And we have seen Haitian immigrants subjected to electronic monitoring and public humiliation, including the deeply troubling case of Pierre Damas Bell,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: a young Haitian college student whose family described the profound distress he experienced after being placed on an ankle monitor

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: simply for existing in this country while seeking safety.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: These are not criminals.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: These are our families.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: These are workers.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: These are our neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: There are so many stories like these.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: So many families who followed every rule, did everything right, and still paid the highest price unimaginable.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: This is what TPS termination means in real life.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: It's literally life or death.

chapters.summary: Council Member Louis says about 350,000 Haitians nationwide held TPS, including 40,000 in New York City, and that those protections are now gone. She cites ICE arrests in New York City and says Mayor Mamdani raised TPS devastation with President Trump.
chapters.title: Council Member Lewis cites TPS and ICE statistics for Haitian New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: An estimated 350,000.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Haitians nationwide held TPS, 40,000 right here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Those protections allowed people to work, support their families, and build lives in our communities.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Today, those protections are now gone.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: While Haiti remains consumed by gang violence, with 1.47 million people displaced and 5.8 million facing food insecurity, the country, our neighbors, fled is

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: no safer today.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: It's actually worse.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And the consequences are being felt right here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: In July, ICE arrested 919 people in New York City, nearly twice the number just three months prior.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: More than three quarters had no criminal history.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: None.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Even Mayor Mamdami recognized what is at stake, convening his third meeting with President Trump yesterday,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: this time at Gracie Mansion, raising directly how TPS termination has devastated several industries in our city, including hospitality, health care, and faith-based communities.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: If the mayor of New York City is bringing this message to the president, the least we can do is go on record in support of restoring these protections.

chapters.summary: Council Member Louis says Haitian New Yorkers are part of the city's fabric and deserve dignity, not fear. She urges colleagues to support Resolution 626 and calls on the Senate to pass S.4814.
chapters.title: Council Member Lewis urges support for Resolution 626

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Haitian New Yorkers are part of the fabric of this city.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: They have cared for our seniors, staffed our hospitals,

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: hospitals, raised families, and enriched every borough they call home.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: They deserve to live with dignity, not in fear.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For Pierre Richard, for every family that has paid an unbearable price, they deserve TPS.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: For the 40,000 TPS recipients in New York City who wake up every morning wondering if today

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: is the last day here in the United States is troubling.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I urge my colleagues to support Resolution 626 and call on the United States Senate to pass and the President to sign Senate Bill S-4814.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Madam Chair.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks Council Member Louis and offers condolences to her family. She then turns the hearing over to committee counsel to administer the oath before administration testimony.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación thanks Lewis and calls administration to testify

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: Thank you, and thank you for introducing this very important piece of legislation.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: And my condolences to your family.

utterances.speaker: Farah N. Louis
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to the committee council to administer the oath before we hear from the mayoral administration.

chapters.title: Council staff administers affirmation to administration panel

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We will now hear testimony from the administration.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: We will hear from Moya Commissioner Faiza Ali, as well as Lorena Lucero.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Before we begin, I will administer the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Panelists, please raise your right hand.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Do you affirm to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth before this committee and to respond honestly to council member questions?

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: You may begin when ready.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Faiza Ali introduces herself as head of the Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs. She says New York City's sanctuary status since 1989 has been foundational to trust between immigrant communities and local government.
chapters.title: Commissioner Faiza Ali introduces herself and sanctuary trust

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Good morning, and thank you, Chair Encarnacion and Councilmember Farrell-Lewis, for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: My name is...

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: My name is Faiza Ali and I'm the Commissioner for the New York City Mayor's Office of Immigrant Affairs.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Since 1989, New York City's sanctuary status has been foundational to the trust between our immigrant communities and local government.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Our city's local laws have helped strengthen public health and safety, empower immigrant New Yorkers to access city services, and ensure that they can participate meaningfully in civic life.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali describes what sanctuary protections mean in practice, including going to hospitals and entrusting children to public schools without fear. She says increased federal immigration activity has heightened fear and disrupted families.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali describes immigrant community fear and service access

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That trust is something that I've experienced firsthand through conversations with community organizations on the ground, one-on-one conversations with immigrant leaders and impacted families, visits to immigration court, and canvassing across the city.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Those experiences have made clear to me that these protections are not abstract policies.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: They shape whether people feel safe going about their daily lives.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: For an immigrant New Yorker, that can mean going to the hospital with confidence, knowing that their immigration status does not determine their ability to access care.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It can mean entrusting their child to our public schools, knowing that city resources and property cannot be used for civil immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That assurance is especially critical today, as increased activity by federal immigration agencies has heightened fear in immigrant communities and disrupted the lives of families and neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Responsive government requires us to continually examine the processes and safeguards we have in place to protect New Yorkers.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali explains that Mayor Mamdani signed Executive Order 13 on February 6, 2026, directing six agencies to audit interactions with federal immigration agencies. She says the order also established the Interagency Response Committee, or IRC, chaired by the First Deputy Mayor.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali explains Executive Order 13 and IRC creation

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: On February 6, 2020,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Mayor Mamdani signed Executive Order 13, directing six agencies, ACS, DOC,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: DOHMH, DOP, DSS, and the NYPD, to conduct comprehensive audits of their internal policies relating to interactions with federal immigration agencies,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: update protocols and guidance where needed, and identify opportunities to strengthen implementation of our local laws limiting or barring city agency participation in federal civil immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: New York City Health and Hospitals voluntarily agreed to participate in the audit, and while New York City Public Schools was not included in EO-13, the agency proactively began its own internal review independent of the formal audit process.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The executive order also established the Intra-Agency Response Committee, or IRC, which coordinates a citywide response to crises.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The first deputy mayor serves as chair of the IRC in direct consultation with the chief counsel to the mayor and city hall,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: special advisor for strategic coordination and operations to the FDM, and myself with support from the Corporation Council and the Law Department.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali says the May audit found local laws generally working as intended while identifying areas for improvement. She highlights increased federal activity at shelters, more detainer requests, expanded federal agencies involved, and aggressive tactics.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali summarizes audit findings on federal activity

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: In May, the City published a report of audit findings and recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The findings confirmed that overall, our local laws are working as intended, while also identifying areas where we can strengthen policies both citywide and within individual agencies.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Throughout this process,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We have emphasized the importance of ongoing accountability and review, as well as broadening reporting to ensure that our local laws continue to be implemented effectively as federal activity in our city and nationwide evolves.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The audit found a dramatic increase in federal immigration-related activity targeting city shelters between January and August 2025.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It also revealed a significant uptick in civil immigration detainer requests to city law enforcement agencies, an expanded set of

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: federal agencies involved in civil immigration enforcement, and increasingly aggressive and misleading tactics by immigration authorities.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali reports that the city updated guidance on reporting federal immigration requests and on non-local law enforcement access to city property. She says the six audited agencies plus H&H and Public Schools have completed or made significant progress on recommendations.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali reports progress on citywide guidance and protocols

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Informed by the audit findings, Mayor Mamdani adopted three sets of recommendations to strengthen the city's implementation of our local laws.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I'm pleased to share that we have made significant progress on implementing each of these recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: First, the city updated its guidance on reporting requests for information and assistance from federal immigration authorities to ensure that every agency interaction with federal immigration authorities is accounted for.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: This guidance was issued to all agencies in June.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Second, the city updated its guidance and best practices on non-local law enforcement access to city property and lots.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: This guidance was also issued to city agencies in June.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The six city agencies subject to the audit, as well as New York City Public Schools and Health and Hospitals,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: have completed their updated access to property protocols, which will be issued by the end of the month, and are now working to ensure that staff are trained on these policies.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Third, the six city agencies subject to the audit, as well as health and hospitals, have completed or made significant progress to fully implement the adopted agency-specific recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: New York City Public Schools has also been meeting regularly with the IRC to monitor enforcement activity and strengthen preparedness.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali details ACS progress, including stronger review of orders of protection and monthly audits of family court reports for improper immigration status references. She says ACS incorporated these practices into trainings and supervision.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali details ACS audit implementation

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I wanted to take a moment to highlight a few examples of the progress our city agencies have made in strengthening their protocols and implementing audit recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The Administration for Children's Services has strengthened its practice of reviewing determinations for seeking orders of protection if the safety of the children and caregiver can be met otherwise when there are potential negative

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: immigration consequences for the parent.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The agency has incorporated this practice into its trainings, into its meetings with family court legal services, and throughout the supervision process.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: ACS has also established a process through which the agency will review a set of court reports from every borough family court legal services unit each month to audit them for inappropriate references to a person's immigration status.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali says DOC's Correctional Intelligence Bureau now reviews federal law enforcement requests to identify their purpose and elevate them to the legal division. She also says the Department of Probation reinforced limits on immigration status in pre-sentencing reports and improved detainer reporting.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali details DOC and DOP audit implementation

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The Department of Corrections Correction Intelligence Bureau has instituted enhanced review of requests for

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: from federal law enforcement agencies to clearly identify the purpose of these requests and appropriately elevate to the legal division to ensure that they are not in furtherance of civil immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The Department of Probation has reinforced through trainings and its academy limitations on inclusion of immigration status

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: in parts of pre-sentencing investigation reports, which do not require this information under state regulation.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: DOP has established a process for regularly submitting reports that document, track, and publicly post a number of detainer requests it receives to strengthen compliance with local laws on reporting.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali says DOHMH is finalizing post-incident protocols and new facility signage. She says DSS issued revised protocols and best practices for shelter and provider staff when non-local law enforcement appears at facilities.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali details DOHMH and DSS audit implementation

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The Department of Health and Mental Hygiene is finalizing post-incident protocols, including notification to individuals and their counsel when appropriate, and working to install

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: New facility signage.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The Department of Social Services has issued revised protocols and best practices to ensure shelter and provider staff are prepared for when non-local law enforcement may show up at their facilities, incorporating what we learned from the

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: period of intense activity at shelters in the first half of 2025.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali says NYPD is on track to complete updated protocols on detainer requests, property access, and joint task forces. She says NYPD has begun implementing protocols for 911 calls involving federal immigration authorities and completed an email audit of task force officers.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali details NYPD audit implementation

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The New York Police Department is on track to complete updated protocols and policies related to detainer requests, access to property, and joint task forces.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: In addition, NYPD has begun the implementation of protocols in response to 911 calls about the press.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: of federal immigration authorities or relating to immigration.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The NYPD has also completed its email audit of task force officers to ensure their compliance with local law.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The email audit is currently under review.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Relatedly, the NYPD is on track to release new protocols to assess information requests that are made through the joint NYPD federal task forces with federal law enforcement.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali says NYC Health and Hospitals issued guidance for when ICE brings individuals to H&H facilities and centralized best practices for staff interactions with federal immigration authorities. She says Public Schools expanded guidance to after-school programs, field trips, and ICE presence near schools.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali details H&H and Public Schools audit implementation

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: New York City Health and Hospitals has developed and issued guidance for when ICE brings an individual to an H&H facility for medical care.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It has also centralized and issued best practices, as well as a flow chart for when staff interact with federal immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And finally, New York City Public Schools has strengthened its guidance for staff if non-local law enforcement is present on school grounds.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The guidance has been expanded for the first time to include after-school and weekend programs, off-site activities like field trips, and what to do if ICE is nearby a school, particularly during arrival and dismissal.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali thanks agency partners and emphasizes ongoing cooperation and continuous improvement. She says work is not finished and MOIA will continue through the IRC to guide agencies and educate the public.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali thanks partners and outlines ongoing work

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I want to thank all of our agency partners and really emphasize the cooperation on this effort from all of them, the careful work that they have done to implement these recommendations, and the ongoing conversations around continuous improvement.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That collaboration gives me confidence in our approach.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: But our work, of course, is not finished.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: City agencies will continue to complete the implementation of

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: of adopted audit recommendations, reviewing and updating their policies as needed.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Through our role in the IRC, MOYA will continue to provide guidance on preparing for and responding to impacts on our immigrant communities, while working with colleagues at sister agencies to educate the public about our laws.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: As federal enforcement practices and tactics evolve, our city government must remain responsive.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The Executive Order 13 audit was one step in that direction.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: This administration is closely monitoring the escalation of civil immigration enforcement activity and responding to the needs we see on the ground, especially when it comes to the interactions our city agencies

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: and federal immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It is our responsibility to support and maintain trust with all New Yorkers, including our immigrant communities.

chapters.summary: Commissioner Ali expresses support for Resolution 626 and says federal termination of Haiti TPS has created fear and economic instability. She describes MOIA's Haitian Response Initiative, multilingual FAQ, outreach, rapid response clinics, and legal support hotline.
chapters.title: Commissioner Ali supports Resolution 626 and Haitian response

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And before I conclude, I also want to briefly discuss and express support for Resolution 626, sponsored by Councilmember Farrell Lewis, calling on Secretary of Homeland Security to designate Haiti for temporary protected status.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The federal government's termination of TPS for Haiti has created fear, confusion, and anguish in our Haitian communities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It has resulted in Haitian New Yorkers losing access to work authorization and economic stability, families becoming afraid to send their children to school, and small businesses seeing fewer patrons and typically active communities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: commercial corridors.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: In addition to advocating for the restoration of TPS, the Mayor and MOIA have also advocated for deferred enforced departure for Haitian New Yorkers affected by the termination of TPS.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We will continue to push for these protections while supporting Haitian New Yorkers and other TPS holders here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: At MOIA, we have worked across the administration and with our community partners, including organizations that are part of our Haitian Response Initiative, to ensure impacted New Yorkers know their rights and have access to legal support.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We are also working to address increased food insecurity and other immediate needs as Haitian New Yorkers who have lost work authorization transition into life without status.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We have developed a comprehensive FAQ available in multiple languages, expanded community outreach, distributed resources on the ground, and stood up rapid response clinics to bring legal services directly into impacted communities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And we encourage those who are impacted to call MOIA's free, safe, and confidential immigration legal support hotline

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: at 1-800-354-0365, where trained staff can connect people with trusted legal assistance in their preferred language.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: New York has always been a city where immigrants come not only to build a future for themselves, but to build a future for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Our administration will continue to make sure that immigrant New Yorkers

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: know that we will stand up for them, that we will defend their rights, and we will fight to protect their families.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks Commissioner Ali, acknowledges Council Member Aviles, and begins questioning. She asks about the responsibilities of each IRC member, and Ali explains the IRC is a coordinating body chaired by the First Deputy Mayor with senior staff support.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks Commissioner Ali about IRC member responsibilities

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you, Commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I also want to acknowledge that we've been joined by Councilor Aviles.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And now we get into the good stuff.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So first and foremost, thank you for detailing all of the folks that are a part and make up the IRC.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Can you go into a little bit about what each one of their responsibilities are as it pertains to the IRC?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair, for that question.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The IRC, as you mentioned, and I have mentioned my testimony, was established through Executive Order 13, and it's a coordinating body.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It coordinates the city's response to federal crises and impacts.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The members of the IRC include the FDM, who serves as chair of the committee,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: in direct consultation with the chief counsel, to the mayor and city, our special advisor for strategic coordination and operations, Bida Moustofi, and myself as MOIA commissioner.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The committee's broader membership also includes other senior level staff.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And some of our responsibilities include helping to coordinate the implementation of Executive Order 13's

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: recommendation, but it also includes supporting agencies as they review and strengthen their policies, their protocols for reporting, and training.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We see

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: this as an ongoing responsibility to continue to provide support to agencies because of the changing federal immigration enforcement environment.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks how often the IRC will review contracts and data-sharing agreements to protect New Yorkers' data privacy. Ali says the audit reviewed technologies and vendors for data risks and confirmed required identifying information law provisions were included.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about IRC review of contracts and data sharing

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So how frequently do you feel like the IRC will review contracts, data sharing agreements between the city and third parties to ensure data privacy for New Yorkers?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yeah, thank you for that question as well.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And I do want to just pivot back because I want to make sure we also highlight that the completion of the audit doesn't mean a completion of the IRC's work.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And just want to stress that that is ongoing.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: With respect to contracts, this was also part of an ongoing review.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: As part of the audit, the IRC asked several agencies to examine specific technologies and vendors that could present potential data risks, data sharing risks.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And we have said for the technologies and vendors that...

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The IRC has reviewed, the audit confirmed that agencies included the necessary identifying information law writer and other contract provisions pertaining to data sharing limitations that is required by local law.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: As I mentioned up top, the IRC is going to continue to monitor these issues and work with agencies on updating their practices as things evolve.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación follows up to confirm that the IRC review includes examining the systems themselves, not just contract language. Ali confirms that is correct.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación follows up on examining data systems

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And that includes examining the systems themselves, right?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Not just the contractual language or for the data sharing with vendors.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That's correct.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether state representatives sit on the IRC. Ali says no state representatives are on the IRC, but the city communicates with state partners informally through MOIA, City Hall, and the Attorney General's office.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks whether state representatives sit on IRC

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Does the IRC interact with the state or is there any state representatives that are on the IRC?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: There aren't any state representatives that are on the IRC, but we do continue to work with our state partners in communicating the impacts both on the ground and any policy changes.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And does that happen formally through the IRC to state partners, or is it informally through the members of the IRC?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yeah, it's informally through the members of the IRC.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Much of the work that MOIA does in collaboration with the Office of New Americans, and then the direct communication that our City Hall office has with the governor's team, along with the attorney general.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether the IRC will consider more severe penalties for city workers who violate sanctuary policies. Ali says failure to implement protective laws will not be tolerated and employees may be subject to discipline.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about penalties for sanctuary violations

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And in addition to some of the things that the IRC will continue to consider, will one of those things involve more severe penalties for city workers who violate the sanctuary policies and regulations?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yeah, a failure to implement the city's laws that protect our neighbors is a failure that we will not tolerate.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So city employees who fail to comply with the applicable sanctuary policies and reporting requirements may be subject to discipline.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether NYC Public Schools will be formally incorporated into the IRC. Ali praises the collaboration, noting regular meetings, updated guidance before the school year, translated Know Your Rights flyers, and a multilingual comic book.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about incorporating NYC Public Schools into IRC

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I know you mentioned a lot of work with the New York City Public.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: schools as kind of like it being voluntary on their end.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Is there any,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Are you looking to formally incorporate them into the work of the IRC moving forward?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We're really pleased with the work that MOYA and IRC are doing in collaboration with New York City Public Schools.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We meet regularly with them to review their policies and protocols and focus on what resources that they may need to support students and families.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And, you know, as I mentioned, although that New York City Public Schools was not specifically identified in EO13, the department did conduct its own internal review and issued updated guidance ahead of the first day of school.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Some of the work that we do that I'm really proud to highlight between MOYA and New York City Public Schools is particularly working on resources for immigrant families.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: at a really critical point as we face increased immigration actions.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: NOIA rights flyers have been updated and are being translated in New York City Public Schools 14 languages.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We are

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Really, I want to uplift the partnership with the Project Open Arms team.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: They do an incredible job in collaborating with us, but also making sure that parents have the information that they need.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I don't know if folks have seen, there's been some press coverage of the collaboration between our offices on a comic book, on a Noya Rights comic book that was developed and is also available in multiple languages.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: This is really an opportunity for us to meet students where they are and making sure that we're providing materials that are both accessible and age appropriate.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And then finally, on the school protocol, MOIA has worked alongside the IRC and New York City Public Schools to update their policies that govern their interactions with non-local law enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: This is really critical because it provides clear guidance to staff and frontline staff on how to respond and protect families and help them understand the protections that are in place.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación comments that the Know Your Rights comic book is a double-edged sword: useful but sad that it is necessary. She says her office distributes it during outreach and applauds its creation.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación comments on MOIA's Know Your Rights comic book

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I, the comic book is like those double-edged swords.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: It's like, it's great that we have it, but it's also very sad that we have it.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So, you know, I applaud it.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We have it in our office.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We give it out during, you know, outreach sessions and resource tabling.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: But it's just a sad reality that we've come to that.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: But I do applaud them as well for creating it.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether all city agencies were told which federal agencies are now involved in civil immigration enforcement before reporting interactions. Ali says the audit identified nontraditional agencies like FBI, HSI, and ORR, and agencies were asked to report broadly.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about federal agencies in civil immigration enforcement

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In terms of the EO-13 findings, the audit essentially asks agencies to look at any interactions with federal agencies that were related to immigration,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: even when those agencies had not historically played a central role in civil immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So were all city agencies given information about which federal agencies are now looped into civil immigration enforcement prior to reporting on these actions, on these interactions?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yes, during the audit, we identified that federal agencies beyond the traditionally associated agencies with civil immigration enforcement, like the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Office of Refugee

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Resettlement, were all playing somewhat of a role.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We've asked agencies to take a broad approach in reporting their interactions with federal agencies.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And in other words,

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We want agencies to report anything that they think can be potentially related to immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And our goal here is really to capture as completely

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: a picture as possible.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks how the audit identified key issues to review. Ali says it combined data analysis, external oversight, stakeholder engagement, historic reporting gaps, DOI findings, and site visits to shelters.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks how audit identified key issues

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: How do you feel that the audit identified those key issues to be reviewed?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That's a great question.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: It really was a combination of a few different things, data analysis, external oversight, and I want to really center our stakeholder engagement and conversations we had with advocates.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: You know, we've analyzed through the IRC city data on interactions with federal immigration authorities, including detainer requests and in-person incidents at shelters and other facilities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We looked at and reviewed historic reporting data that we know revealed significant gaps and previously unreported incidents.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We also considered the findings of the Department of Investigation's report on DOC and NYPD, which you referenced in your opening, and looked to get input from advocates, journalists, and other stakeholders.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Agencies were, as we mentioned, were also asked to report and, you know, over-report, be over-inclusive in their reporting of any interaction that they had with federal authorities, which is how we uncovered many of these interactions.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And then finally, members of our IRC team also conducted site visits and visiting shelters directly to assess the vulnerabilities and, you know, and any other protocols.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación notes that Council Member Joseph has joined and says she will ask two more questions before allowing Joseph to speak on the resolution. She then asks about the timeline for releasing all citywide guidance, and Ali says both guidance documents were issued in June.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación notes Joseph's arrival and asks guidance timeline

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In your, also I just want to note,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: that we've been joined by Councilmember Joseph.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm going to ask about two more questions, and I'm going to allow her to make a statement on the resolution we're hearing today.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: In your opening statement, you mentioned a timeline.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I believe you said that some of the updated citywide guidance was released as of June, and some might be released by the end of this month.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I believe that was in relation to the public schools, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I was trying to write as fast as possible.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: For all of the citywide guidance, is there a timeline for when those will be released?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So both citywide guidance, the guidance on reporting requirements and guidance as well on best practices for non-local law enforcement access to city property and lots, both were issued in June.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yeah.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks who will oversee the IRC's issuance of updated guidance. Ali says the IRC and the Law Department will oversee issuance and implementation.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks who oversees IRC guidance issuance

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And who will oversee the IRC's issuance of the updated guidance?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The IRC, along with our partners at the law department, will oversee the issuance of citywide guidance and implementation of those updated policies and protocols.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether the city anticipates needing additional resources for this work. Ali says current work relies on existing agency structures and resources, but MOIA continues to assess resource needs.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about additional resources for IRC work

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Does the city anticipate needing any additional resources to conduct this work?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: At this time, our work is focused on existing agency structures and resources to support the implementation and really the ongoing work.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: But, Chair, you've heard me say this before.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: MOIA continues to assess resource needs, and that's something that we're closely monitoring as well.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether agencies have been instructed to alert MOIA if they need support or training. Ali confirms that agencies can raise needs through MOIA and the IRC, and that training is required for public-facing city employees and contracted employees.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks how agencies request training support

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And so will agencies, have they been instructed, like if they need additional support or they find that they need

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: help making sure that this happens throughout their agency as far as trainings, for example, that's something that they will alert MOIA and MOIA will bring to the IRC and then...

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And training is required for all public-facing city employees, contracted employees, and others.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And so that is something that we will continue to work with individual agencies on.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks when MOIA and the IRC will revise previously published reports and issue unpublished reports as indicated by EO recommendations. Ali says Local Law 228 reports for FY26 are published and amended reports are still in progress.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks when MOIA and IRC will revise reports

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And lastly, before I hand it over to the council member, when will MOIA and IRC revise previously published reports and issue unpublished reports as indicated by the EO recommendations?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: The local law 228 report.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: for FY26, I'm pleased to say, have been completed and are published.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And MOIA and the IRC are continuing their work on the amended reports identified in the EO recommendations and will notify the Council as soon as those are ready.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación turns the floor to Council Member Rita Joseph for remarks on the resolution. Joseph thanks the chair and begins her statement in support of S.4814.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación turns to Council Member Joseph for remarks

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Council Member Joseph, ready?

chapters.summary: Council Member Joseph speaks as a daughter of Haiti and representative of Haitian New Yorkers, describing the 2010 earthquake and the promise of TPS. She says Haiti remains unsafe, TPS was stripped away, and S.4814 is not charity but recognition that Haitians are neighbors and future.
chapters.title: Council Member Joseph delivers remarks supporting Resolution 626

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: This is remarks in support of Reso 4814.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So just want to read remarks in support, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: So I stand here today as a daughter of Haiti and as the representative of thousands of Haitian New Yorkers who built their lives in this city in good faith under the protection this country promised them.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: 16 years ago, an earthquake took 300,000 lives in less than a minute.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Out of that devastation, America made a promise, temporary protective status, a chance to work, to raise a family, to breathe without the fear of being sent back into chaos.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That promise still matters today because the chaos never left.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Nearly a million and a half Haitians displaced, millions facing hunger, gangs controlling entire neighborhoods of the capital.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And yet this past year, that protection was stripped away.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: First by an agency, then upheld by the Supreme Court.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I've walked the streets of Little Haiti and Flatbush.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: I've watched vendors disappear.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Storefronts go dark.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Parents are afraid to send their children to school.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That is what fear does to a community.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That is what we're asking.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: to reverse.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: S-4814 is not a favor.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: It is not charity.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: It is a recognition of a simple truth.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Haiti is not safe and the people who fled it are not a threat.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: They are our neighbors, our caregivers, our small business owners, our future.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: The House had already passed its version.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Now the Senate must act and the president must sign.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: In Haiti's motto, it says, L'union fait la force.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Unity makes strength.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That is the spirit of Little Haiti.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: That is the spirit of this city.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: And today, this council stands behind 40,000 New Yorkers who are counting on us not to look away.

utterances.speaker: Rita C. Joseph
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks about ACS's plan to audit court reports for improper immigration status references. Ali says ACS established monthly reviews by family court legal services deputy borough chiefs and the first audit is under review through the IRC.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about ACS court report audit

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So I want to get into some questions around ACS.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: ACS indicated that they plan to audit their court reports to review any improper inclusion of immigration status.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Has that audit occurred?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yes, that audit, I'm just making sure I have the correct information in front of me.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Yes, ACS has established an ongoing process where each of the five family court legal service deputy borough chiefs, that they actually review a set of those court reports every month.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: These reviews are going to be logged.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: They'll be assessed to audit for improper inclusion of immigration status.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And the first monthly audit has been completed and it is under review.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay, and so the next steps for that is that it will be reviewed, and that is being reviewed through the IRC, just to be clear?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: Through conversations with the IRC and the agency, correct.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether ACS's required annual refresher training for staff and providers will take place this year. Ali says ACS is creating refresher trainings to begin in January 2027 and MOIA will review and support the rollout.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about ACS annual refresher training

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: They're also required annual refresher trainers for all of ACS and providers'staff on compliance and reporting requirements.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Will the training take place this year?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: That is currently in process as well, and ACS is working to create its refresher trainings and implement it starting January 2027, and it's incorporated in the updated protocols.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: MOIA is going to be involved in reviewing and supporting the rollout of that training.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You read my mind.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: That was the next question.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether ACS has instituted audit procedures including retraining and discipline for repeat violations. Ali says ACS is working to establish retraining procedures on the same timeline as refresher training, starting early next year.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about ACS retraining and discipline procedures

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I know they also indicated that they plan to

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: institute audit procedures that included retraining if violations are found and disciplinary procedures if they are repeat violations.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Have those audit procedures been instituted?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: ACS is working to establish a procedure for retraining and it will be on the same timeline as the refresher training.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So starting early next year.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether MOIA and the IRC will ensure ACS implements a procedure to seek written consent from children's attorneys before outreach to immigration authorities. Ali says ACS now uses a consent form and MOIA will continue working through the IRC.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about ACS written consent from attorneys

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So I know that they also indicated that they were developing a procedure to seek written consent from attorneys for children prior to outreach to immigration authorities on an individual's case.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Will MOIA and the IRC be involved in ensuring that those recommendations are implemented?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I think first it's important for us to highlight some of the progress that ACS made on this front.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: ACS now uses a form to obtain written consent from attorneys for children before doing outreach to immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And MOIA will continue to work through the IRC to work with ACS along with some of the other agencies to implement these policies moving forward.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Gotcha.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación moves to DOC and asks what enhanced review of federal law enforcement requests means. Ali says DOC's Correctional Intelligence Bureau will identify the purpose of requests and elevate them to the legal division for review.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about DOC enhanced review of federal requests

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So now I'm going to move over to DOC.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: What does it mean for DOC to institute an enhanced review of requests for federal law enforcement agencies?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: As I mentioned in my testimony, in practical terms, it means that DOC's Correctional Intelligence Bureau will institute

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: and review their policies that clearly identifies the purpose behind any law enforcement request for information

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: or assistance, including requests that are made through the task forces, and then elevate those requests to their legal division for review.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks when DOC will discontinue daily reports to ICE not required by law and who will confirm it. Ali says DOC no longer sends those reports and oversight will be conducted through the IRC, though she will follow up on a formal timeline.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks when DOC stopped daily ICE reports

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: When will DOC discontinue daily reports to ICE that are not required by federal, state, or local law?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And who will be responsible for confirming this discontinuation?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So this has already taken effect.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: DOC no longer sends these reports.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: As you mentioned, these were reports that were not required by state law.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: And this is the ongoing oversight of this will be conducted through the IRC.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And is that on a monthly basis, do you know?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Is there like a reporting?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Like how do you envision that happening through the IRC?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I will get back to you on that.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I don't know if there's a formal sort of timeline, but we do have regular communications and maintain regular communications with not just the six audited agencies, but other agencies as well.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks who was responsible for the DOC email audit. Ali says DOC is working with its IT team to set up the audit and targets completion by the end of the year.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks who conducted DOC email audit

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You also mentioned in your opening about the email audit that occurred.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Can you talk a little bit about who was responsible for that audit within the department?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So DOC is currently working with its IT team to set up the audit and is targeting for that audit to be completed by the end of the year.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks what the audit of technology vendors and third parties entailed. Ali says the IRC team worked with agencies to review contracts and vendors, but she will follow up on whether every vendor storing or accessing city information was identified.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación asks about audit of technology vendors

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And you also mentioned some audit of technology vendors and third parties.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: What did that entail, that audit?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So that was part, I believe it was reflected in our audit findings as well.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: a review of contracts and of different vendors at different agencies.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So the IRC team worked with the agencies to review those documents.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And did it identify every vendor that stores, processes, or has access to information maintained by city agencies?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: I will have to get back to you on that.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación pauses her questioning to allow Council Member Aviles to ask questions. Aviles thanks the chair and begins her round.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación pauses for Council Member Aviles' questions

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Okay, and so before we move on to the next.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Set of questions.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I'm going to pause and allow Councilmember Aviles to ask her questions.

chapters.summary: Council Member Aviles follows up on the IRC's review of contracts and data-sharing agreements, asking about the breadth and scope of surveying actual data in systems. Ali says the review looked at data flows and contract protections, and MOIA will follow up with details on what was surveyed.
chapters.title: Council Member Aviles asks about IRC data and contract review scope

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I just want to ask a follow-up question to the earlier subject of the IRC reviewing contracts and the data sharing agreements.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Where you noted that the process also looked at the actual data.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: So I was just curious about if possible you could explain a little more detail about the breadth and scope.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Of that surveying of actual data in the systems and over what period of time?

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: So I will get back to you on terms of the timeline, but as I mentioned that the technology

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: and the vendors that were reviewed from the audit.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: We were looking for a few things, but one thing in particular, to make sure that the necessary identifying information law writers were present and that other protections were present in the contracts as well.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
utterances.text: But we can follow up and get you additional details on the timeline and the time frame.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: Yeah, I guess what I'm really interested in learning is what did a surveying of samples actually look like with the breadth of contracts that I'm sure the city engages in?

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear that, you know, those elements are in the contracts, but I would love to know if when you look at the data actually across some of those systems, what you found.

utterances.speaker: Alexa Avilés
utterances.text: So happy to talk about that some more.

utterances.speaker: Faiza Ali
