chapters.summary: Rosa Cohen-Cruz of Bronx Defenders says she has testified repeatedly about sanctuary violations by DOC, NYPD, and ACS. She welcomes EO 13 but says DOC misreads the statute by transferring people with certain convictions without a judicial warrant and by counting instant-arrest convictions.
chapters.title: Rosa Cohen-Cruz of Bronx Defenders testifies on DOC sanctuary violations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Encarnacion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: My name is Rosa Concruse, and I'm the Director of Immigration Policy for the Bronx Defenders.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: I've testified before this council alongside many of the same people right here and my immigrant justice colleagues about half a dozen times over multiple years about persistent violations of our city's sanctuary laws,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: particularly on the part of the Department of Corrections, NYPD, and in at least one instance, ACS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: We welcomed and were encouraged by Mayor Mumdani's early action by issuing EO-13 and auditing compliance with our laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Some of the findings were shocking to us, especially the finding that the Department of Corrections had been sending a daily list of non-citizens with BSC conditions to ICE despite that not being required by law.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: And we are glad to hear that that practice has been discontinued.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: However, as we have been testifying about for many years, we are really concerned about the Department of Corrections reading of the statute and their belief that they are in compliance, even though it goes against the clear

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: text of the plain reading of the statute itself.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Particularly, they're reading that they are allowed to transfer custody of individuals with VSC convictions without a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: And they're reading that conviction qualifies even if it is the instant arrest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Neither of those come part with the plain reading.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: of the statute and this council should, or this administration should update their guidance, but also this council needs to pass legislation to make sure that the department is being held accountable,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: as well as the other agencies named in the audit.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: We need lasting legislative solutions, not just executive action, even though we are very grateful to see it happen.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: And there are three bills that we've continued to come back to this council about.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: One is Intro 209, the Immigrant Trust Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: The other is Intro 395 and 396.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: All of which address accountability for following the sanctuary laws and would fix the loopholes in existing laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rosa Cohen-Cruz
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Brittany Brown of New York County Defender Services says the audit revealed DOC routinely sent daily lists of people in custody to federal authorities without mayoral approval. She describes a case where a correction officer facilitated an ICE interview request and says the audit must go beyond formal requests.
chapters.title: Brittany Brown of New York County Defender Services testifies on DOC information sharing

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: My name is Brittany Brown.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: I'm the supervising attorney of the Collateral Consequences Unit at New York County Defender Services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Thank you to the Committee on Immigration for holding this public hearing on this necessary and historically overdue audit and recognizing that meaningful sanctuary protections need to exist in practice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: In examining DOC's practices, the audit identified information sharing practices, as Rosa mentioned, that were unknown and had received little public scrutiny.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Most notably, the audit found that DOC affirmatively and routinely transmitted information concerning individuals in custody to federal authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Specifically, DOC sent federal law enforcement agencies daily lists containing information about individuals in custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: The significance of this finding cannot be overstated.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: It is unimaginable that in a sanctuary city, a city agency would preemptively cooperate with federal immigration authorities without any approval for such a policy from the mayor's office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: We are grateful that this was discovered during the audit, and it shows how this administration is handling the situation differently from previous ones.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: But it also illustrates how difficult it can be for the council, advocates, and the public to understand how information actually moves through DOC without meaningful and sustained oversight.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: There have been countless hearings where DOC has testified in front of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: council, but not once was this policy ever disclosed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: We've also seen concerning and arguably unlawful examples of DOC personnel facilitating direct contact between people in custody and federal immigration authorities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: In one recent case, while our client was in DOC custody, a correction officer approached him with a form asking whether he wished to participate in an interview with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Put more simply, DOC personnel was facilitating ICE's access to a person in city custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: We believe this type of facilitation violated our city's detainer law, which sharply limits DOC's use of city personnel and resources to assist federal civil immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: This example would not have been caught by the audit and shows why the audit's analysis needs to go beyond formal requests.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Briefly, I just want to also highlight the Department of Probation's collection and inclusion of immigration information in pre-sentence investigation reports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: The city should determine what immigration information is actually required to be in these pre-sentence reports and where

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Department of Probation can obtain or verify necessary information without contacting ICE and what safeguards can ensure that the pre-sentence investigation process does not become a conduit for federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Brittany Brown
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Deborah Lee of the Legal Aid Society says sanctuary laws protect all New Yorkers but the audit found serious gaps, especially DOC's continued coordination with ICE. She says DOC responded to 24 ICE detainer requests and urges passage of Intro 396, Intro 209, and Intro 395, plus public quarterly EO 13 reports.
chapters.title: Deborah Lee of Legal Aid Society testifies on DOC-ICE coordination

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Encarnacion and members of the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: My name is Deborah Lee, and I'm the attorney in charge of the Immigration Law Unit at the Legal Aid Society.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: I'm testifying on behalf of legal aid, including our criminal defense practice, whose attorneys witness firsthand the consequences when the Department of Corrections and NYPD collaborate with federal immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: New York City should be proud of its sanctuary laws and their role in protecting non-citizen New Yorkers, safeguarding due process, promoting access to essential services, and building trust in government institutions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: All New Yorkers are safer when people can access schools, shelters, health care, courts, and other public services without fear of immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: The EO-13 audit highlights serious gaps that require attention, though.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: Most concerning is DOC's continued coordination with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: The audit found that DOC responded to 24 ICE detainer requests by providing release notifications and facilitating transfers to federal custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: No New Yorker's information should be shared with ICE absent a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: We urge the Council to reintroduce and pass Intro 396 to close this loophole.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: We also urge the Council to pass the New York City Trust Act, Intro 209 and Intro 395.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: Sanctuary laws are only meaningful when they can be enforced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: New Yorkers whose rights are violated should have a clear path to accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: Accountability also requires transparency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: We urge the administration, Moya, to make the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: the quarterly EO-13 reports public so New Yorkers can assess whether sanctuary laws are being faithfully implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: Finally, Legal Aid supports Resolution 626 calling for the restoration of TPS for Haiti.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: As ICE intensifies efforts to detain and deport Haitian nationals following the termination of

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: TPS protections, Haitian New Yorkers face family separation, loss of work authorization, and removal to a country still experiencing profound instability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: At a time of escalating federal immigration enforcement, New York City must strengthen its sanctuary laws, close remaining loopholes, promote transparency, and ensure meaningful accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Deborah Lee
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

chapters.summary: Josh Epstein of Brooklyn Defender Services thanks the mayor and IRC for the audit and says it highlighted gaps in detainer laws. He raises concerns about third-party data sharing, NYPD's Domain Awareness System, and jail phone systems storing voice prints and biometric data.
chapters.title: Josh Epstein of Brooklyn Defender Services testifies on data surveillance risks

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: My name is Josh Epstein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: I'm the Director of Immigration at Brooklyn Defenders Queens Office.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you so much to the committee and to Chair Encarnacion for hosting today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: We are grateful to the Mayor for signing Executive Order 13 and to the IRC for their work to strengthen New York City's compliance with local sanctuary laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: And completing a thorough audit of agency practices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: This critical process helped elucidate the ways federal immigration enforcement is targeting New Yorkers and highlighted the ways that the city can tighten protections to make New Yorkers safe for all.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: The City Council has taken steps to limit city agencies'ability to facilitate civil immigration enforcement, such as New York City's groundbreaking detainer discretion laws.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: And the Executive Order 13 report highlighted the interpretation and implementation of these laws have left gaps, and these gaps expose immigrant New Yorkers to ICE detention.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: The City Council, as my colleagues have mentioned, can pass the New York City Trust Act, which will strengthen the enforceability of New York City's existing detainer protections.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Brooklyn Defenders is grateful that as part of the audit, the data sharing agreements between the Department of Corrections, the NYPD, and third-party technology vendors were reviewed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Relying on outside vendors in an era of mass data, accumulation by big tech companies, and the federal government carries serious risks for immigrant New Yorkers, but also

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: the civil rights and liberties of all New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: We're also glad the IRC will continue reviewing the contracts for data sharing agreements between city agencies and third parties.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: We urge the mayor's office and the IRC to review NYPD's policies regarding audits of the domain awareness system, and the domain awareness system is NYPD's surveillance platform.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: That serves as a hub for aggregating data under NYPD's control, and this vast system is available to officers on their cell phones, and it has not had an independent audit in over a decade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: In correctional settings, the use of digital surveillance technology also raises risks of data leaks that could lead to immigration enforcement in violation of our city's sanctuary policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: The jail phone call systems operated by Securus not only record jail phone calls, but also store voice prints, a form of biometric data, on every individual who uses the system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: This includes family members, friends, community members, children of people experiencing incarceration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: And this problem is compounded by the sheer volume of data that the city allows the NYPD and DOC to collect.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: And while asking minimal questions about who is accessing it, why, and how it is being used, we can't meaningfully protect it from misuse.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you to the committee for hosting this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Josh Epstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Whitney Bronstein of Immigrant Defense Project says DOC has allowed ICE to detain New Yorkers from Rikers without judicial warrants and misreads the statute on convictions. She says NYPD reporting compliance is good but non-reporting elements and 911 call incidents remain unaddressed, urging passage of the Trust Act and Intros 395 and 396.
chapters.title: Whitney Bronstein of Immigrant Defense Project testifies on DOC and NYPD gaps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Good morning and thank you to the Committee on Immigration and Chair Encarnacion for holding this hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: My name is Whitney Bronstein.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: I am Senior Attorney for Community Defense at the Immigrant Defense Project, which is an organization focused on fighting for justice for all immigrants, including those targeted by the criminal and immigration legal systems.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Executive Order 13 has taken critical steps in auditing city agencies and their compliance with local laws around communication and collaboration with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: However, I would like to highlight key issues yet unaddressed by the report which have undermined due process and caused irreversible harm to New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: First, the Department of Corrections is squarely prohibited by our laws from transferring New Yorkers to ICE custody absent a judgment of enumerated conviction for one of the 178 laws within our very serious crimes carve-out and a judicial warrant.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: However, DOC has routinely allowed ICE to show up at Rikers to detain New Yorkers directly from their cells without a moment of freedom, without a judicial warrant, under a mythical distinction that they are not honoring a detainer but solely communicating with ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Communication that is not obligated for them to do and has the effect of separating families on the precipice of being reunited.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Additionally, under Statute 9131, as well as DOC's own 2019 operations order, when DOC is considering honoring a detainer, convictions of relevance are those that precede the instant arrest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: DOC has long misinterpreted this to allow them to take into account

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: charges flowing from the instant arrest, which can include people who have no conviction at all, certainly not ones that precede the current incarceration that they're experiencing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: This is the basic misreading of this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: statute that must be addressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Second, I'd like to address the report's recommendations regarding the NYPD.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: It was great to hear from the committee and from Commissioner Ali earlier this morning that NYPD is up to date on its reporting and compliance with those requirements under our local law 10-178.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: However, non-reporting elements of that section have not been

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: addressed, such as the use of resources or taking direction from the Department of Homeland Security, primarily in furtherance of immigration enforcement, were not addressed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: With regard to 911 calls, we heard earlier this morning about the way in which reporting requirements have been implemented by the OMPD, which is great to hear.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: However, incidents such as the May 2026

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: rate at the Wyckoff Medical Center continue to occur.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: We need recommendations that address actions, not solely reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: For this reason, we urge the Council to pass the New York City Trust Act and the not yet reintroduced bills 395 and 396 to ensure that our laws are enforced in order to protect the rights of immigrant New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Whitney Bronstein
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación thanks the panel and notes she is now lead sponsor of Intros 395 and 396. She commits to moving them through the legislative process, working with advocates to strengthen the wording, and holding a hearing with DOC.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación commits to moving Intros 395 and 396

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you to all of you for, and some of you are part of conversations that we were talking about these three bills in particular, 209, 395, 396.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I am now the sponsor, lead sponsor for 395 and 396 and have committed to move it forward through the legislative process.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I'm hoping to get this in front of DOC and have a hearing as soon as it goes through this process that I will continue.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And I'm committed to working with many of you to look at how we can strengthen the wording of those particular.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: pieces of legislation and we'll see how we get to on the other side of that and I appreciate

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: you all meeting with me and also supplying me with some questions some of which I was able to get to today some of which I think are more appropriate to ask directly to DOC but I appreciate all of you for your testimony today thank you

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación calls the next panel: Monique Francis from CUNY Citizenship Now, Laura Adams from The Door, Maria Posadenti from Safe Passage Project, Rodney Souvenir from the Haitian American Lawyers Association, and Joshua Santangelo from Children's Law Center.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación calls second public panel

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I will now call up the next panel.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: We have Monique Francis from CUNY Citizenship Now.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Lola Adams from The Door.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Maria Posante from Safe Passage Project.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Rodney Souvenir from the Haitian American Lawyers Association and Joshua Santangelo from Children's Law Center in Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Hello, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And as soon as everyone is situated, we can begin.

chapters.summary: Monique Francis of CUNY Citizenship Now describes its free legal services since 1997 and its work with Haitian TPS since before the 2010 earthquake. She recounts early large TPS application events and current partnerships for Know Your Rights and family preparedness sessions.
chapters.title: Monique Francis of CUNY Citizenship Now testifies on Haitian TPS services

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: Thank you, Chairperson Encarnacion and members of the Immigration Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: I would also like to express gratitude to Councilmember Farrah Lewis for the invitation to share this testimony today and for her advocacy in pushing forward

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: Resolution 626 that calls for Congress to extend TPS for Haitian New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: My name is Monique Francis.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: I'm the Executive Director at CUNY Citizenship Now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: CUNY Citizenship Now has remained a lifeline for New York City's immigrant communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: We provide trusted, free, and confidential legal services since 1997.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: For three decades, our attorneys and paralegals assist eligibility for immigration benefits, and we help New Yorkers navigate application process, including TPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: The infrastructure has become even more important during these moments of rapidly changing immigration policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: When misinformation and fear

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: can leave families vulnerable, and especially in this moment when the federal administration has forgotten the contributions of immigrants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: Our work with Haitian TPS began long before the first major earthquake devastated Haiti in 2010, and we have remained steadfast not only with Haitian TPS,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: but also with the Haitian Family Reunification Program, asylum support, and most recent, Haitian parole programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: I want to take you back to 2010 when I was working as the budget manager for Citizenship Now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: On January 28th, less than two weeks after the first earthquake, Citizenship Now, in partnership with Legal Aid Society, held the city's first large group processing TPS application assistance event.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: The event was held at Medgar Evers College with more than 400 Haitians seeking support for this humanitarian relief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: We made a call for volunteers and help for interpreters and translations, and the number of New Yorkers who spoke French and Haitian Creole who reached out to support this event was astonishing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: Within the first few months after the earthquake, CUNY, through our partnerships and collaborations with both state and city government, helped more than a thousand immigrants.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: In June of 2026, with the deadline to end the protections near, our organization has held virtual Zoom sessions offering guidance on other types of legal benefits.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: We have partnered with organizations like Little Haiti BK,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: Haitian American Alliance of New York, and the Haitian Institute at Brooklyn College to provide Know Your Rights and Family Preparedness session.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Monique Francis
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Laura Adams of The Door says the organization handled over 2,500 immigration matters this year, including 614 unaccompanied minors. She reports drops in program attendance due to ICE fear, raises concerns about ORR and ICE targeting foster youth, and says DYCD was excluded from the audit.
chapters.title: Laura Adams of The Door testifies on immigrant youth and DYCD gaps

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: Hello, and thank you for letting me speak here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: And we look forward to sending our full written testimony after today's hearing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: I'm Laura Adams.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: I apologize for my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: The legal program manager at The Door, which is a comprehensive youth development organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: And at the Doors Legal Services Center this year, we've handled over 2,500 immigration matters for youth from infancy to 24 years old, including 614 unaccompanied immigrant minors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: Executive Order 13 is a great first step to ensure immigrant youth have the best success and chance at success at the growth in New York City without the fear of abusive immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: We have observed significant drops in our attendance at all of our programs at the door, including drop-in centers, schools, health clinics, housing assistance, and mental health programs due to fear of ICE enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: And we do want to draw the council's attention to the audit's reports of the continued illegal ICE harassment of staff and participants of our city shelters and of our foster care youth and families in the ACS system.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: The information in the audit on the so-called wellness checks from ICE and DHS agencies for foster care youth is consistent with what we have observed with the collusion between the Office of Refugee Resettlement and ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: to target recently released unaccompanied minors in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: So ORR is definitely part of our immigration enforcement units at this point, and I want to draw attention to the fact that their information sharing policies are problematic here.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: These young people should be able to pursue their immigration cases and live normal lives without the harassment and intimidation from the federal government once they're out of federal custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: We do want to echo concerns that the Department of Youth and Community Development was not included in this audit or in the executive order.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: Protections required for other city departments should extend to protect runaway and homeless youth, especially as hundreds of immigrant youth come to DYCD and their drop-in centers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: The New York City Council has met about DYCD in the past and their information sharing policies with ORR and ICE, so it's very relevant to this.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: And they've acknowledged the sensitive nature of the information sharing on unaccompanied minors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: So finally, we do urge the codification of the protections in Executive Order 13 through the passage of legislation like the New York State Trust Act and offer our support as well for the resolution in support of TPS for Haiti.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Laura Adams
utterances.text: So thank you for your time and consideration.

chapters.summary: Maria Posadenti of Safe Passage Project tells the story of Dee, an unaccompanied minor in ACS custody who missed immigration court and was later arrested by ICE after being placed on Long Island. She says ACS failures led to months in adult ICE detention and urges concrete protections for children in ACS custody.
chapters.title: Maria Posadenti of Safe Passage Project testifies on ACS custody case

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Isabel Ortega Romero
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Thank you for this opportunity today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: My name is Maria Posadenti, and I'm a staff attorney at Safe Passage Project, a nonprofit that provides free legal representation to immigrant children facing deportation in New York City and Long Island.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: We're grateful that city officials are taking steps to ensure that city agencies protect the immigrant New Yorkers who rely on them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: And we want to warn that more must be done to ensure that unaccompanied immigrant children in the custody of New York Administration for Children's Services, ACS, do not fall through the cracks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: I have represented a young person who I will call Dee since January 2026.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Dee is an unaccompanied minor who was found to be a destitute child and placed in ACS custody after his abusive older brother kicked him out of his home.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: I met Dee after he was ordered deported because ACS neglected to inform the caseworkers at his placement facility that he was scheduled for an immigration court hearing, which he missed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: We petitioned for special immigrant juvenile status while we moved to reopen his immigration court case.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: ACS moved him from a Manhattan placement to a group home on Long Island where he repeatedly expressed feeling unsafe and unhappy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: We also learned he had a pending criminal case in Suffolk County, which made him vulnerable to being turned over to ICE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: We warned ACS about this and advocated for him to be moved back to New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Sadly, our fears were realized.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: In May, Suffolk police took Dee from his group home to a police station for questioning where Ice waited outside to arrest him.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Ice claimed that Dee was an adult, not a 16-year-old child, despite the overwhelming evidence presented to them proving his age.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Ice held Dee in adult detention for...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: for over three months while we filed a habeas petition to get him released.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Finally, in August, ICE quietly moved Dee to a shelter for immigrant minors without conceding their error.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Dee suffered immeasurable harm during his months in adult ICE detention, including being attacked by other detainees and being placed in solitary confinement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: Had ACS placed D within NYC instead of out on Long Island, I believe that the city's measures to limit information sharing between local police and ICE would have stopped him

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: from being turned over to immigration officials, in turn saving him from months of suffering as a child in adult ICE custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Maria Posadenti
utterances.text: I urge the members of this committee and the mayor's administration to remember Dee's story as you work to implement the findings of this audit and take concrete steps to ensure that children in ACS custody like Dee are truly protected.

chapters.summary: Rodney Souvenir, president of the Haitian American Lawyers Association of New York, strongly supports Resolution 626 and S.4814. He notes the House passed its version with bipartisan support and describes how TPS uncertainty affects Haitian families in Flatbush, Canarsie, and beyond.
chapters.title: Rodney Souvenir of Haitian American Lawyers Association supports Resolution 626

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Good morning, Che and Canacion and members of the Committee on Immigration.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: My name is Rodney El Pepe Souvenir, and I'm the president of the Haitian American Lawyers Association of New York.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify in strong support of Resolution 626, sponsored by Councilmember Farrah Lewis, calling upon the United States Congress to pass

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Senate Bill 4814, designating Haiti for temporary protective status, TPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: I want to thank Councilmember Lewis for her leadership and her steadfast commitment to the Haitian community here in her district and across our city.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: On April 16, the House of Representatives passed its version of this legislation, H.R.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: 1689, with bipartisan support.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Senate Bill 4814 would give the Senate the chance to finish that work and allow eligible Haitian nationals to continue living and working lawfully in this country.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: After the Supreme Court allowed the termination of Haiti's TPS to move forward, Congress is now the clearest path to protecting these families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Nationwide, roughly 350,000 Haitians depended on TPS.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Many of them are our neighbors here in New York City, in Flatbush, Canarsie, East Flatbush,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Cambria Heights, and beyond.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: They are nurses and home health aides, teachers, small business owners, lawyers, and parents of Americans.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: American citizen children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Many have lived here for more than a decade.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: As lawyers, we see every day what uncertainty does to these families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: We see people afraid to go to work, afraid to renew a lease,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: afraid to plan a future.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: We have had to tell parents that they have to make a choice of whether to take their children into the certain dangers that exist currently in Haiti or separate and leave their children with a trusted friend or family member here in the States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: TPS exists for exactly the conditions that Haiti faces today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Political instability, widespread violence, and the humanitarian emergency.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Sending people back into that danger is neither lawful in spirit nor humane in practice.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: This council has long stood with New York City's immigrant communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: I respectfully urge the committee to adopt Resolution 626 and add New York City's voice to the call for Congress to pass Senate Bill 4814.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Without delay, our families cannot wait.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rodney El Pepe Souvenir
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Joshua Santangelo of Children's Law Center's Youth Guardianship Project says immigrant clients fear entering government buildings, including courthouses, and guardians refuse fingerprinting due to ICE fear. He urges passage of the Trust Act and continued Know Your Rights materials.
chapters.title: Joshua Santangelo of Children's Law Center testifies on SIJS and distrust

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: Good morning, Chair Encarnacion and the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: My name is Joshua Santangelo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: I am the supervising attorney for Children's Law Center's Youth Guardianship Project, which does SIDG work, Special Immigrant Juvenile Status Work.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: Firstly, I want to applaud this administration and the council's efforts to protect our immigrant populations against the propagation of rules from the federal government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: As this body is aware, the federal government's recent actions have created real and irreparable damage and fear within our immigrant communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: Many of the clients that we interact with are afraid to enter any governmental building, including state and city courthouses.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: Many of our cases hit snags when guardians of our clients refuse to get fingerprinted at state courthouses due to fear of ICE presence.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: So far, we've been able to overcome that by accompanying guardians, finding outside fingerprinting resources, and making applications to waive fingerprints where applicable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: But the emotion of distrust present within these communities is palpable.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: This administration's efforts to protect our communities and separate the city government's intentions from that of the federal government are admirable, but there's still more work to be done.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: There's so much distrust in any governmental body that is present within immigrant communities that we serve.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: And we have seen this through Moy's efforts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: to disseminate Know Your Rights materials and through directors by city administrations that there is an intention to separate the city from the federal government.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: However, as this committee has commented on, there's just not enough attorneys present in this city to do the work that is necessary.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: So we encourage the passage of the Trust Act and similar legislation to

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: both try to limit how many cases are actually moving into the court system by holding the administrations that are passing information to ICE accountable and also to continue to propagate know your rights materials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: I would like to have commented on the

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: resolution as well, but I will just submit the written testimony in the interest of time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Joshua Santangelo
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación asks whether Santangelo supports the resolution, and he says yes. She asks him to put that on the record and thanks the panel.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación confirms Santangelo's support for Resolution 626

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And my assumption is you are in support of the resolution.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You can put that on the record.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you all for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Chair Encarnación calls the next panel: Lady Zela Rosa from La Colmena, Gisela Marroquin and Van from Mixteca, Julio Santo Domingo from the International Rescue Committee, and Sandra Jourdainet. She notes one person may be at another hearing and calls Karina from NYLPI to take a space.
chapters.title: Chair Encarnación calls third public panel

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I will now call up Ladies de la Rosa from La Colmena.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Jusela from Misteca Organization.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Van also from Misteca.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Julio Santo Domingo, IRC.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And Sandra.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Deuda.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Jio Day?

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Judo Day.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Judo Day.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: I believe one of the folks that I called up may be at another hearing.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: So I'm going to call up Karina from New York Lawyers for the Public to take her space.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: And you may start.

chapters.summary: Gisela Marroquin of Mixteca says the organization has served Latinx and Indigenous communities in Sunset Park for 26 years. She calls for public multilingual data-sharing policies, accountability for DOC's past daily ICE reporting, and firm deadlines for implementing protections.
chapters.title: Gisela Marroquin of Mixteca testifies on data sharing and accountability

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: My name is Gisela Marroquin.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: I'm the Managing Director of Mixteca, a community-based organization based out of Sunset Park, Brooklyn.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: I appreciate the opportunity to provide testimony this morning as this committee analyzes the Executive Order 13 report of audit findings, its information and learnings, and gets ready to make further recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Mixteca has provided services to the Latinx and Indigenous communities in Sunset Park for 26 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Our service delivery model centers mental health and well-being and is delivered through trauma-informed practices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Our reach now expands beyond Brooklyn and community members across all five boroughs come to Mixteca, particularly seeking information and legal support around immigration policies and understanding their rights as immigrants, parents, and caretakers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: With so much information out there, our community members trust us to identify accurate and up-to-date information that protects them and their families.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: We're happy to hear that changes have been made across several agencies, and we appreciate the continued efforts to ensure the safety of our immigrant neighbors.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: The audit identified gaps, and the following are specified and measurable oversight mechanisms we hope the council could require to close the gaps and demonstrate accountability.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Every city agency should have clear, public, and easily accessible data sharing policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Given the Department of Corrections'history of daily jail reporting sharing with ICE, there must be a strong accountability for noncompliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Once finalized, these protocols

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: should be published in multiple languages so that all New Yorkers can understand them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Policies regarding ICE access to city facilities must be shared with community-based organizations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Many community members come to Mixteca before seeking medical care or other basic services because they aren't sure whether an interaction with the city agency or a shelter could expose them or their family member to immigration enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Unauthorized ICE access to hospitals, public buildings, parking lots, or schools violates community trust and can keep families from obtaining essential care and services.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: The Council should establish a firm deadline for agencies to finalize and implement these policies and the mechanisms to track their implementation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: If I could just go, lastly, while we commend Mayor Mamdani's proactive signing of Executive Order 13, we urge the City Council to consider ensuring these protections

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: and their implementation are not only dependent on a single administration or one mayor's commitment, and the Council should examine which of these protections should be made into permanent law with clear enforcement, reporting, and oversight mechanisms that are transparent and accessible.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Gisela Marroquin
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Van of Mixteca says most agencies complied with EO 13 but some protocols were not followed. Van calls for a communication plan to inform immigrant New Yorkers through community-based organizations and for quarterly updates and audits.
chapters.title: Van of Mixteca testifies on communicating EO 13 protections

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Council Members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: Thank you for the opportunity to testify today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: My name is Van.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: I'm the community organizer at Mixteca, a community-based organization in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, that has served immigrant, Latin, and indigenous communities for over 25 years.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: After reviewing the Executive Order 13 audit recommendations, it was great to see that the majority of the city agencies were able to comply with and enforce the changes that the mayor implemented.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: But as the report also showed, there were a few instances in which these new Executive Order 13 protocols were not followed.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: The proposed recommendations call for strengthening documentation, reporting, and transparency, which I agree with, but it is unclear how this information will be shared with immigrant New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: A plan to inform immigrant New Yorkers about the new policies and procedures should be developed, particularly targeting community-based organizations where many people in our community obtain their information and updates.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: With the recent changes to public charge policies and ongoing threats facing our community, it is essential to ensure that there is consistent communication and regular updates for immigrant New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: The recommendation suggests that city agencies should endure quarterly audits, which should be followed by proposals to enhance protections for our immigrant community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: Additionally, there should be quarterly plans to share updates, findings, and changes to policies and procedures with all New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: At Mixed Deck Up, we provide continuous Know Your Rights workshops and resources to our community members.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: During these presentations, we do our best to inform our community members and keep them updated on policy changes that may affect them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: Some of the presentation materials we provide are the IRW presentations from the Mayor's Office of Immigration Affairs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: It would be incredibly helpful if MOYA's IRW presentations could include updates on how EO-13 is strengthening protections for immigrant New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: I would like to thank the committee for the continued work supporting our immigrant New Yorkers, and I hope you are able to develop a communication plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Van
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Sandra Jourdainet of Catholic Charities' Haitian Response Initiative describes its culturally and linguistically responsive legal services. She says TPS has ended for over 330,000 Haitians nationwide and asks the Senate to pass S.4814 and DHS to halt arrests and deportations of former TPS holders.
chapters.title: Sandra Jourdainet of Catholic Charities testifies on Haitian TPS loss

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: My name is Sandra Jourdainet, and I am the supervising attorney for the Haitian Response Initiative at Catholic Charities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: I would like to thank Councilwoman Farrah Lewis for inviting us to speak today and for sponsoring Resolution 626.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: And thank you, Councilwoman Encarnacion, for having us here today.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: The Catholic Charities Haitian Response Initiative was established in 2022 to respond to the growing legal and humanitarian needs that Haitian New Yorkers faced.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: HRI provides culturally and linguistically responsive immigration legal services, meaning that the staff is Haitian or Haitian American, and we all speak Haitian Creole, which helps with...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: Cultural sensitivities and for New Yorkers to tell us their story.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: We assist with asylum, temporary protected status, employment authorization, special immigrant juvenile status, adjustment of status, and other forms of humanitarian relief.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: Our work extends beyond the far walls of our offices.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: We conduct Know Your Rights presentations, legal clinics, immigration screenings, and community outreach throughout New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: We work with faith-based organizations, elected officials, and trusted partners.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: We meet Haitian New Yorkers where they are and provide critical information and services in both Haitian Creole and English.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: Today, as we know,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: TPS has ended.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: And more than 300,000, 330,000 Haitians nationwide had faced the loss of temporary protective status, placing their families who have lived, worked, and paid taxes and raised children in the United States at risk of losing their work authorization

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: and their protection from deportation.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: Haitian TPS holders are our neighbors, healthcare workers, home health aides, caregivers, business owners, students, and parents in this community.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: The impact reaches far beyond immigration status.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: The psychological toll can also be very profound.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: People who have spent years building stable lives are now suddenly facing horrible conditions.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: The thought of sending them back to Haiti, where it's very dangerous and they have mixed status families, where the parents are TPS holders, but their children are U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: Citizens.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: And now they're deciding whether I take my children to this dangerous country or do I leave them here with people that they don't really know.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: We're asking that the Senate bill passes 4814 because it's really important to make sure that we protect our Haitian immigrants in the United States.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sandra Jourdainet
utterances.text: We're also asking that DHS halts arrests and deportation of affected former TPS holders and restore humanitarian protection where legally available.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

chapters.summary: Julio Santo Domingo of the International Rescue Committee says IRC has served 10,000 Haitian clients in four years, including 5,700 in New York and New Jersey. He describes Haiti's gang violence and food insecurity and supports Resolution 626, sharing a client's story.
chapters.title: Julio Santo Domingo of International Rescue Committee supports Resolution 626

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Canacion and the committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: My name is Julio Santo Domingo.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: I'm a deputy director of the New York office of the International Rescue Committee.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: I am here to express our support for Resolution 626.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: The IRC, or the International Rescue Committee, supports both internally in the United States and, of course, New York, and also internationally the Haitian population.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: In the last four years, we have served 10,000 Haitian clients overall, 5,700 through New York and New Jersey alone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: So it's a reflection of how central this population is to our organization.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: In RSC's country program in Haiti, here's the reports.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: Every day, reflect the profound security and humanitarian challenges the country faces, including sexual violence, kidnapping, displacement, combined West Bridge food insecurity, armed gangs have control across 90% of the capital and beyond,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: restricting humanitarian access.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: Over half the population, 5.8 million people, do not have enough to eat, a crisis expected to deepen as an approaching unneeded pattern threatens to drive food insecurity even higher.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: For Haitian families who have built their lives in the United States,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: The loss of TPS have devastating consequences, creating uncertainty surrounding not only their ability to remain and work in the U.S., but also their ability to work in the U.S.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: Also, the stability of the communities.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: These are not simply immigration matters.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: They are deeply human concerns that affect families, livelihoods, and the ability of individuals to plan for their futures.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: One of our clients, for example, who fled Haiti and arrived in 2023 with her two children, is just one of the great examples.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: Of a New Yorker that's facing this crisis right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: TPS would have protected her from returning to Haiti and from detention in the U.S., but this protection from four Haitians was ended before she could submit her application.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: We at DRC have helped her continue to in other means, such as applying through asylum.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: However,

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: You can finish your sentence.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: The loss of TPS is potentially being set back to harm.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: It threatens not only the safety of current generations, but the hope of the children and the generations to come.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Julio Santo Domingo
utterances.text: So thank you for your time today.

utterances.speaker: Elsie Encarnación
utterances.text: Thank you, and thank you for clarifying that you are not the same IRC that we were talking about the whole time that we were having this hearing.

chapters.summary: Karina Bistegui-Adler of New York Lawyers for the Public Interest supports EO 13 and H&H's voluntary participation. She asks H&H to track ICE medical clearance requests, for the IRC to partner with immigrant patient advocacy organizations, and for the city to support the Safe Access to Care Act.
chapters.title: Karina Bistegui-Adler of NYLPI testifies on H&H and hospital protections

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair Encarnacion.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: My name is Karina Bistegui-Adler.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: I'm the director of the Health Justice Program at New York Lawyers for the Public Interest.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: We, of course, support Intro 626, but I'm here to testify about Executive Order 13.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: In brief, we support the recommendations that the mayor has adopted and applaud H&H for...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Voluntarily participating in the audit and adopting policies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: H&H is the largest public health system in the country, and I believe that what H&H does will help set the tone for every other hospital in the city, including private and voluntary hospitals,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: many of which are located in immigrant communities and have been involved in incidents of ICE presence and violent enforcement.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Today we have a few recommendations.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: First, as part of the reporting requirement, we ask that H&H track and report any medical clearance requests that ICE directs at treating providers when they are carrying for patients in ICE custody.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: We've heard repeatedly that ICE brings people to H&H for medical clearance or demands written medical clearance after apprehending and injuring New Yorkers on the street and before transferring them to immigration detention centers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: We know from our extensive work documenting and litigating medical neglect in immigration detention centers that the continuity of care after discharge is not being honored.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: If true, we fear that these letters can contribute to the continued neglect and inhumane detention of New Yorkers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Careful tracking, reporting, and auditing of these requests could be the difference between detained New Yorkers returning to their community or languishing in immigration detention centers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Second, we hope that the IRC will formally partner with immigrant patient advocacy organizations like Health Justice for New York behind us, NLP, as they consider policies, implementation, and ongoing reporting.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: And lastly, we asked the committee pass a resolution to support state bill, Senate bill 10494, the Safe Access to Care Act.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: The bill would require every hospital in New York, public or private, to adopt written protections right now.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Only H&H is stepping up to volunteer, but this bill would close the gap for everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: Thank you again for your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Karina Bistegui-Adler
utterances.text: I look forward to continued collaboration to support the health and safety of New Yorkers.
